Precondition: does this row's notion of deployment map onto a macOS LaunchAgent? It holds by mapping 'the response that claims the change is shipped' onto the one place this repo makes a shipped-claim: the console output of `interstice install`. It applies, and it fails there. lib/install.js:142-145 catches a launchctl load failure, prints `launchctl    load failed: <msg>`, and then unconditionally prints `launchctl    loaded` on the very next line; install() also returns true unconditionally (install.js:146) and bin/interstice.js:71 follows with 'Now run: interstice doctor'. Add the same `launchctl list` assertion as a doctor check in lib/doctor.js beside the existing 'LaunchAgent installed' check so a loaded-vs-merely-present plist is distinguishable.

Every finding in this batch was reached through file reads and read-only inspection, never through compilation: cat and sed on lib/install.js, lib/server.js, lib/daemon.js, lib/reader.js, lib/amazon-session.js and lib/state/companions.js; git grep for credential shapes; ps, launchctl list and stat for the process and mtime evidence; and curl against the daemon that was already running. Zero builds and zero compiles were started, so zero Mac CPU was spent on a problem that reading found.

This layer was not touched: no background build was started during this audit (no run_in_background call, no nohup, no `&`), so there is no PID to track or reap and `pgrep` has no survivor to report. The only long-lived process involved, node pid 859, was already running under launchd before the audit began and was left untouched. Noted in passing, since it is the project's own version of this discipline: the daemon writes logs/interstice.pid at lib/daemon.js:91 and unlinks it at :160, the panel writes logs/panel.pid and adopts an existing window's pid rather than spawning a rival (lib/panel.js:170-184, :218-223), and lib/cdp.js:86 SIGKILLs a browser that never opened its debugging port.

This layer was not touched: both shell channels stayed responsive for the whole audit. Every Bash invocation returned normally, including the ones issued while the reading rung's Chrome processes were up, so there was no starvation signature to diagnose and no retry loop to break out of.

No single command was allowed to run unbounded. Every network call carried an explicit cap (`curl --max-time 8`, raised to 40 only for /api/todos and /api/reading, which cross into Notes and the Kindle store); the slowest command in the audit was the 40-second-capped /api/todos probe, which returned 200 application/json inside the cap. No foreground command exceeded one minute. The product holds the same discipline internally: 34 explicit `timeout:` options across lib/ bound every execFile subprocess.

Nothing was deleted during this audit and no rm was run or requested. Checked the repo for the punt shape too: grep across README.md and docs/*.md finds no instruction to run rm, and the only `rm -rf` string in the tree is test/companions-control.test.js:26, an assertion that a shell-injection payload is neutralized rather than a deletion. The product's own deletions all target its own scratch state, never user data: mkdtemp temp dirs in lib/amazon-session.js:76,102,160 and lib/ocr.js:87, its own LaunchAgent in lib/install.js:154, its own compiled hotkey bundles in lib/hotkeys.js:57-59, and its own reader profile cookie store at lib/reader.js:676 (path built from READER_PROFILE at :659), which is additionally guarded at :663-666 so a working session is never destroyed before a replacement is known to exist. uninstall() ends with 'logs left in place' (lib/install.js:167).

The project's one real credential need is Amazon sign-in, and it is deliberately never asked for, typed, or held. lib/amazon-session.js:16-18 states 'No Amazon credential exists in the vault, the account authenticates with a passkey, and a tool that fills in passwords is a tool that has to hold them', and carryAmazonSession (lib/amazon-session.js:112-161) moves the already-sealed amazon.com cookie rows between Chrome profiles without decrypting anything; when that fails the fallback is a real sign-in window the person drives (lib/server.js:367-396). No credential is hardcoded: `git grep -nE "sk-|ghp_|AKIA|BEGIN .*PRIVATE KEY|Bearer <token>|postgres://user:pw@"` across tracked files returns zero, and config apiKey is null. The one config read that touches a key, lib/state/anki-discovery.js:50, reads AnkiConnect's own published addon config to learn the endpoint the user configured, which is a dependency integration point rather than a filesystem hunt for a user secret.

This layer was not touched: no NoActiveGrantError occurred because the secrets broker was never invoked during this audit and the repo contains no broker call site. grep for 'secrets-driver', 'SecretsDriver', 'NoActiveGrant' and 'get_secret' across the tree (excluding node_modules, .git and logs) returns only two prose mentions, docs/GOAL_LOOP_STARS_READER_2026-08-17.md:181 and docs/STARS_NOTES_2026-08-19.md:154, neither of which is a call or a routed-around error.

No credential-shaped string exists in any tracked file: `git grep -nE "sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{16,}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|Bearer [A-Za-z0-9._-]{24,}|postgres://[^:]+:[^@]+@"` returns zero hits, as does a grep for key/token/secret/password literal assignments; config/interstice.config.default.json:40 sets apiKey to null. The one place real credential material lives on disk, the reader's Chrome cookie store holding the live Amazon session, is untracked and ignored: `git check-ignore -v logs/reader-profile/Default/Cookies` prints `.gitignore:2:logs/`, and `git ls-files logs` is empty. Grepping logs/*.log and logs/*.jsonl for the same credential shapes plus at-main, session-token and x-amz- returns zero. Nothing decrypts a cookie either: sessionMark returns hex of the still-sealed encrypted_value (lib/amazon-session.js:87-104) and its only caller compares two marks for equality in memory (lib/reader.js:673-675), never logging or rendering them.

Every one of the ~35 route handlers in lib/server.js:81-538 reads or mutates state with no authentication and no authorization check of any kind: grep for origin, authoriz, token, csrf, referer and password across lib/server.js and lib/focus/stars-routes.js returns zero hits, and the dispatcher at :542-545 keys purely on `${req.method} ${url.pathname}`. Loopback binding (:573) is not a substitute, because readBody (:36-51) JSON-parses the body regardless of content-type, so any page the user visits can issue no-preflight cross-origin POSTs that mutate real state: POST /api/cards/answer reschedules Anki cards (:163-171), POST /api/todos/toggle writes todo state (:428-440), POST /api/reading/input types keystrokes into a signed-in Amazon session (:317-343), and POST /debug/companions, /debug/submit and /debug/end drive the daemon (:497-537). Verified live: `curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7420/api/queued -H 'Content-Type: text/plain;charset=UTF-8' -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' -d '{"text":""}'` was accepted and routed (400 'empty', the handler's own validation at :115, no auth rejection), and `curl -H 'Host: attacker.example' -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' /api/health` returned 200, so neither Origin nor Host is validated and DNS rebinding would also read responses.
fix: In the http.createServer handler at lib/server.js:540, before dispatching, reject any request whose Host header is not `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`, and reject any request carrying an Origin header that is not the daemon's own origin (a same-origin fetch from /panel sends no Origin on GET and its own origin on POST). Additionally require a per-install token, generated at install time into config/interstice.config.json and injected into the served HTML, on every mutating method and on all /debug/* routes.

Its remote settability is reported under SEC-004, not here.
